# SOP-100 — Centrifugal Pump Preventive Maintenance

**Applies to:** Horizontal centrifugal pumps, Units P-101 through P-108, main process water loop.

## 1. Inspection Interval

Routine visual inspection is required every 30 days. A full preventive
maintenance service (bearing lubrication, seal inspection, vibration
analysis) is required every 180 days, or immediately if any of the
Section 3 alert thresholds are exceeded during a routine inspection.

## 2. Standard Operating Parameters

- Normal discharge pressure range: 4.5 - 6.2 bar.
- Maximum continuous bearing temperature: 85 degrees Celsius.
- Maximum allowable vibration velocity (ISO 10816 Zone B): 4.5 mm/s RMS.
- Rated flow rate: 250 cubic meters per hour at rated head.

## 3. Alert Thresholds Requiring Escalation

If any of the following are observed during inspection, the unit must be
flagged for immediate maintenance review and the shift supervisor notified
before the pump is returned to unattended operation:

- Bearing temperature exceeding 90 degrees Celsius.
- Discharge pressure below 4.0 bar or above 6.8 bar sustained for more
  than 5 minutes.
- Vibration velocity exceeding 7.1 mm/s RMS (ISO 10816 Zone D).
- Visible seal leakage exceeding 2 drops per minute.
- Unusual cavitation noise at the suction side.

## 4. Corrective Actions

- Bearing over-temperature: reduce load, inspect lubrication, schedule
  bearing replacement within 48 hours if temperature does not recover.
- Seal leakage above threshold: schedule mechanical seal replacement
  within 7 days; do not run the unit dry.
- Cavitation: verify suction strainer is not blocked and NPSH available
  meets the pump curve requirement before resuming normal operation.

## 5. Approval

Maintenance findings requiring corrective action outside routine service
must be signed off by a certified maintenance engineer before the unit is
released back to production.
